text:
Maria Gomez: Heads-up — perf regression surfaced on prod GPU pool after last runtime deploy (v2.3.4). Observed: prefix cache global hit-rate dropped ~18% for tail traffic; GPU cache memory climbs until OOM on two nodes, then fallback to CPU which increases latency. Posting profile snippet and quick numbers.

Aj Patel: ugh. any diffs in keying/normalization in that release? last time a subtle prompt-normalize change exploded unique keys.

Maria Gomez: good call. I diffed the keygen: small change to include "user_id" when prompt.length < 64 to reduce collisions. intent was good but probably increased entropy for short prompts. snippet:

```
// before
key = hash(prefix.text + model_id)
// after (v2.3.4)
if (prefix.len < 64) key = hash(prefix.text + model_id + user_id)
else key = hash(prefix.text + model_id)
```

Maria Gomez: we rolled to prod canary, but high-frequency short prompts are common in a few services — explains drop in hit-rate.

Noah Kim: that explains unique-key blowup. related observation: kernel routing changed to prefer fused-kernel path for shorter sequences, which keeps more KV state per request (we keep local slot refs longer). Combined effect = higher GPU resident memory.

Sam Rao: TL;DR: more unique keys + longer resident KV lifecycle -> fragmentation + OOMs. Suggest two-pronged mitigation: revert user_id addition OR make it tenant-scoped in index (coarser) + aggressive TTL for short prefixes.

Lee Chen: agree. Quick mitigation plan:
- revert key change on canary immediately (rollback)
- add quick TTL patch: short-prefix TTL -> 30s (was 5m) for affected routes
- enable softcap eviction (probabilistic LRU) on GPU cache to avoid instant OOM
Canary at 1% and observe hit-rate / OOMs.

Rachel O'Neill: I'm running a small experiment against canary: two buckets (A: reverted keygen, B: keep keygen + TTL=30s + softcap). initial 30m results: A hit-rate restores ~16% improvement vs prod; B restores ~12% but lowers OOMs by 90%. attaching numbers:
- prod (v2.3.4): hit 42% tail, GPU OOMs = 2/hour
- A (revert): hit 58%, OOMs = 0.1/hour
- B (ttl+softcap): hit 54%, OOMs = 0.2/hour

infra-bot: ALERT: node gpu-17 OOM at 2026-02-12T14:02:11Z — killed runtime-worker pid=4321. kernel=nvaccel-v1. log snippet: 

```
[2026-02-12T14:02:11Z] OOM killer triggered: runtime-worker(4321) rss 18.9G > limit 17.0G
[evict] attempted LRU prune 1200 entries, freed 150kB
[alloc] failed allocate kv_slot=0x7ff...
```

Aj Patel: that log shows evict loop didn't free much — fragmentation. we should move to slab coalescing + opportunistic compaction on soft-evict.

Noah Kim: also check kernel path: fused-kernel keeps larger per-request metadata structures. Possible short-term: route short prompts to unfused kernel path (slightly higher latency but smaller resident KV). I'll add a routing rule that prefers compact kernel for prefix<64 on affected canary.

Sam Rao: experiment matrix proposal (small):
- control: prod v2.3.4
- revert-key only
- ttl+softcap only
- kernel-route compact + ttl
- compaction + softcap + ttl
Measure: hit-rate, GPU resident mem p95, OOM count, p99 latency.

Maria Gomez: sounds good. action items: @Aj rollback keygen on canary now; @Noah add routing override; @Rachel continue A/B and collect p95 GPU mem hist; @Lee prep softcap toggle and slab compaction flag behind feature gate. I'll post a short postmortem draft after we stabilize. :thumbsup:

Lee Chen: doing toggles now, starting canary ramp to 1%.

Rachel O'Neill: collecting metrics, will post charts in ~45m. :bar_chart:

Aj Patel: rolled back keygen on canary. monitoring. :white_check_mark:

Noah Kim: routing override in place for canary (compact kernel for prefix<64).

Maria Gomez: thanks team. quick note for long-term: we should add unit tests that assert cache key cardinality doesn't increase >10% for typical prompt distributions. and add a profiler alert for GPU slab fragmentation.

Sam Rao: +1 on cardinality tests. also recommend adding an adaptive TTL that drops TTL when unique-key rate spikes. :thinking_face:

Maria Gomez: agreed. follow-ups in eng-runtime retro.
